title: Writing
text:
Washington University Political Review
Throughout my undergraduate career, I wrote extensively for the Washington University Political Review in addition to serving as editor-in-chief my senior year. Some of the topics I covered include:

Urban sprawl and transportation in St. Louis
2020 candidates’ housing policy proposals
The economic history of craft brewing in St. Louis
The interaction between political sorting, partisan polarization, and legislative gridlock



Academic Papers
In Spring 2019, I took a graduate seminar in social choice theory. For my final paper, I compared the social choice-theoretic properties of plurality and ranked choice voting.

title: Michael Fogarty
text: I am currently a PhD student in economics at the University of Wisconsin-Madison. Previously, I was a research assistant at the Federal Reserve Bank of Chicago. I graduated from Washington University in St. Louis with a bachelor’s degree in Economics and Political Science in 2019.

title: Research
text:
My research interests include urban economics, public finance, fiscal federalism, political economy and applied microeconomics more broadly.
I was previously a research assistant on the regional team at the Federal Reserve Bank of Chicago.
I have worked with Professor Therese McGuire on several projects related to fiscal federalism in the United States, Canada, Germany, and Spain. Additionally, I have prepared homeworks and lectures for her state and local public economics course for Kellogg MBA students.
My undergraduate honors thesis examined the possibility of correcting sample selection bias with detailed controls, using a large dataset of wholesale used car auctions. My thesis won the Adam Smith Prize for Excellence in Economics.

title: Software
text:
Seasonal Adjustment for Big Data
adjust_data.R implements the seasonal adjustment procedure for Big Data series with short time series history outlined in Tracking U.S. Consumers in Real Time with a New Weekly Index of Retail Trade.


Other Software Tools
importhaver. This R package provides a user-friendly interface for accessing time-series data from Haver Analytics in a tidy format. Requires network access to Haver databases.
